{{Cleanup biography|date=July 2021}}
{{short description|Physicist and philosopher of science}}
'''Jeffrey Bub''' (born 1942) is a [[physicist]] and [[philosophy of physics|philosopher of physics]], and [[Distinguished Professor]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.philosophy.umd.edu/people/bub|title=Jeffrey Bub. Distinguished University Professor|publisher=University of Maryland, Department of Philosophy|accessdate=23 November 2014|archive-date=19 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190219170624/http://www.philosophy.umd.edu/people/bub|url-status=dead}}</ref> in the department of philosophy at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]].<ref>[http://carnap.umd.edu/philphysics/bub.html Jeffrey Bub] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110907115622/http://carnap.umd.edu/philphysics/bub.html |date=2011-09-07 }}, Faculty page, University of Maryland, College Park (downloaded February 23, 2012)</ref>

== Education ==
He obtained his bachelor's degree in pure mathematics and physics from the [[University of Cape Town]]. A scholarship allowed him to work at [[Birkbeck College]] with [[David Bohm]] who had profound intellectual influence on his work.<ref>{{cite journal | url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/0269859022000013346 | doi=10.1080/0269859022000013346 | title=Bub and the barriers to quantum ontology | year=2002 | last1=Peacock | first1=Kent A. | journal=International Studies in the Philosophy of Science | volume=16 | issue=3 | pages=285–289 | s2cid=121610308 | url-access=subscription }}</ref> Bub obtained his PhD in Mathematical Physics from [[University of London]] in 1966. Before taking up his position as professor at the University of Maryland in 1986, he worked at the [[University of Minnesota]], [[Yale University]], [[Tel Aviv University]], and the [[University of Western Ontario]]. He has been visiting professor at [[Princeton University]], Yale University, the [[University of California, Irvine]], the CPNSS at the [[London School of Economics]], the [[University of California, San Diego]], the [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]], and the Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information at the [[University of Vienna]].<ref name="symposia-templeton-cv">[http://symposia.templeton.org/deep_beauty/bios.html#bub CV] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160323005407/http://symposia.templeton.org/deep_beauty/bios.html#bub |date=2016-03-23 }} at John Templeton Foundation (downloaded February 23, 2012)</ref>

His main research interests relate to quantum foundations, [[quantum information]], [[quantum computing]], and [[quantum cryptography]]. In 1998, his book ''Interpreting the Quantum World'' won the [[Lakatos Award]].<ref>[http://users.ox.ac.uk/~everett/biographies.htm#Jeffrey_Bub Short CV, Cambridge University] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161108060621/http://users.ox.ac.uk/~everett/biographies.htm#Jeffrey_Bub |date=2016-11-08 }} (downloaded February 23, 2012)</ref> In 2005 he received the University of Maryland's ''Kirwan Faculty Research and Scholarship Prize'' for his work in the area of quantum foundations and quantum information.

Bub has published over 100 scientific articles; the first of these are three articles authored together with David Bohm and published in 1966 and 1968. In 2010, he published an argument that the famous work of [[John Stewart Bell]] (and, thus, [[Grete Hermann]]) had misconstrued [[John von Neumann]]'s [[Mathematical Foundations of Quantum Mechanics#No hidden variables proof|no hidden variables proof]] of the impossibility of hidden variables in quantum mechanics.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Von Neumann's 'No Hidden Variables' Proof: A Re-Appraisal|year=2010 |last1=Bub |first1=Jeffrey |journal=Foundations of Physics |volume=40|issue=9–10|pages=1333–1340 |doi=10.1007/s10701-010-9480-9|arxiv=1006.0499|bibcode=2010FoPh...40.1333B|s2cid=118595119 }}</ref> The validity of Bub's argument is, in turn, disputed.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Homer nodded: von Neumann's surprising oversight |journal=Foundations of Physics |volume=48 |issue=9 |pages=1007–1020 |year=2018 |arxiv=1805.10311 |last1=Mermin |first1=N. David |last2=Schack |first2=Rüdiger |author-link1=N. David Mermin|doi=10.1007/s10701-018-0197-5 |bibcode=2018FoPh...48.1007M |s2cid=118951033 }}</ref>
